images.caption: Figure 1:ROAM-Bench checks task outcomes and required observations and interactions. Counting mugs across a home requires searching multiple rooms, checking rooms without mugs, and opening a cupboard to find a hidden mug. Independent checks verify the final count, target observations, room coverage, and container inspection.

Figure 2:The 11 task types in five groups, illustrated with recorded camera observations, detail insets, and schematic annotations. Instructions are abbreviated. Relocation shows the target, destination, and placed-object stages of one episode.

Figure 3:Agent interaction and independent evaluation. Retrieval supplements roundtt, a skill produces observations and feedback att+1t+1, and finishing triggers outcome and evidence checks. Saved episode images, a rendered reference object, and a path visualization illustrate the inputs and outputs.

Figure S1:Saved observations from a successful GPT-6-astra relocation episode (scene_148). Rounds 1, 12, 18, and 19 show the initial view, pre-pick view, pre-place view, and post-place view before completion. The episode contains 18 charged actions and 19 rounds.

Figure S2:Relocation across seven models. Left: successive stages over 210 episodes. Placement requires a preceding pick of the same acceptable object. Destination support adds a post-placement check of the released object. Right: pre-pick and post-place views from a successful GPT-6-astra episode.

Figure S3:Human review of exploration evidence across seven evaluated models. Reference images, exploration frames, and action feedback support manually checked object-localization and behavioral judgments. Tiles show paired-judgment availability for 84 recorded cases. Camera thumbnails illustrate the inputs using a GPT-6-astra relocation episode.
